channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Residents Pushing To Place Quantum Campus Referendum On March Primary Ballots
item.description: A referendum in the March primary elections would ask residents near the Quantum Shore development whether local leaders should stop the project. A review is ongoing, but the effort appears to meet signature requirements for ballot placement, officials said.

item.title: Beat Kitchen Sues City, Alleging Discrimination In Riverwalk Concession Award
item.description: The lawsuit alleges city officials weighed race during scoring and privately encouraged a vendor to apply after the deadline.

item.title: Zoomies, Chicago’s 1st Indoor Dog Park And Bar, Is Coming To Avondale
item.description: Zoomies will offer pet grooming, day care and boarding, and two fenced-off dog runs when it opens next summer — as well as a cafe and bar for humans.

item.title: Where Does Your Alderperson Stand On ICE? We Checked All 50
item.description: City Bureau chronicled and categorized Chicago alderpeople's actions and statements regarding protection for immigrant communities and the actions of federal agents in the city.

item.title: Original Rainbow Cone In Beverly Open Despite Morning Break-In
item.description: Police are investigating a break-in early Wednesday at the Original Rainbow Cone in Beverly.

item.title: Bovino Leads Caravan Through Chicago Before Clashing With Evanston Mayor
item.description: Wednesday marked Bovino's second day back on the job in the Chicago area after he left in November.

item.title: With Free Store Volunteer Facing Eviction, Neighbors Work To Keep Her Home For The Holidays
item.description: An organizer at a Washington Park "free store" has created a fundraiser for Porsha Weekly, a mother of four and an "essential" volunteer who recently lost her job and was served an eviction notice.

item.title: Get A Tattoo To Help One Tail At A Time’s Rescue Animals This Month
item.description: Crybaby Tattoo in Pilsen is donating a portion of flash tattoo sales and collecting supplies through December to support the Bucktown animal rescue.

item.title: Vote-By-Mail Registration Is Open For March Primary. Here’s How To Apply
item.description: Chicago voters can now apply to vote by mail for the March 17 primary election, with ballots set to begin mailing out in early February.

item.title: Bears Threaten Move To Northwest Indiana After State Leaders Balk At Arlington Heights Stadium Aid
item.description: In an open letter to fans, Bears President Kevin Warren said the team is expanding its stadium search beyond Arlington Heights due to a breakdown in talks over financial assistance for a previously planned domed suburban stadium.
